questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become more confident at school
How body language works in video meetings
Why Zoom is better than meeting in person
How to give a good speech at work
questions.why: Neil says they'll be asking how body language has changed in the world of online video meetings.

questions.q: How are Sam and Neil recording this programme?
options: On Zoom from their homes
On Skype from different countries
By phone from their offices
Face-to-face in the BBC studio
questions.why: Sam says they're recording face-to-face in the studio, 'which, I am happy to say, we are doing right now'.

questions.q: Why do online meetings often feel more distant?
options: It's almost impossible to make eye contact
People speak much more quietly online
Meetings online are always much shorter
People can't hear each other clearly
questions.why: Neil says making eye contact through a web camera is almost impossible, creating a 'distancing' effect.

questions.q: What is Erica Dhawan's final piece of advice?
options: Always keep your microphone on mute
Smile as much as possible on camera
Slow down and wait before speaking
Look directly at other people's faces
questions.why: She says 'last but not least, slow down' and suggests waiting five seconds before speaking.

questions.q: According to Erica, why should we wait five seconds before speaking?
options: To check that everyone's camera is on
To stop people from interrupting the leader
To make the meeting finish more quickly
To give people time to think about ideas
questions.why: She says it makes sure individuals have time to process the ideas, especially with technology issues.

questions.q: What is Michael Rosen worried about?
options: People laugh and smile less on video calls
People laugh too much during online meetings
People no longer want to meet in person
People spend too long in online meetings
questions.why: He asks if video calls are 'killing off people laughing and smiling' as we do in live situations.

questions.q: According to Erica, why do we laugh less on camera?
options: Because people are more serious at work now
Because nobody tells jokes in online meetings
Screen delays stop us laughing together
Because cameras make people look unattractive
questions.why: She says laughing often happens in unison, and screen delays and seeing our own camera make it less likely.

questions.q: What does Erica suggest to solve this problem?
options: Turning off all cameras during meetings
Planning time for informal chat in meetings
Having fewer online meetings each week
Showing funny videos at the start of meetings
questions.why: She suggests 'creating intentional moments in our meetings for the water cooler effect' – informal chat.
